description: Objects don't unify when an attribute they share is bool in one and number in the other
notes: The spec's rules only say that number and bool each unify with string, and none names bool with number. But it defines unification as finding a type that all the given types can be converted to, the most general supertype in a lattice, and bool and number both convert safely to string, which would give the object {a = "true", b = "x"}. hashicorp/hcl fails to unify attribute a, and then fails the whole unification (unifyObjectTypes in cty/convert/unify.go) instead of trying a map of all the attribute types, which would be a map of strings.
